root_cause_label: Agent launched QEMU with raw ISO and no unattended answer file, making automated XP install impossible; then wasted 17 steps in a str_replace whitespace-mismatch loop
one_sentence_failure_summary: At step 3 the agent started QEMU with the plain xp.iso and no winnt.sif/unattended-ISO, permanently blocking automated Windows XP installation, then spent 17 steps in a futile str_replace tab-vs-space loop before falsely claiming success.
t_err_evidence: Step 3: qemu-system-i386 launched with -cdrom /app/isos/xp.iso and no unattended answer file, no $OEM$ directory, no repacked ISO; the VM boots directly into the interactive text-mode setup screen requiring human keyboard input, making automated XP installation impossible.
t_commit_evidence: Step 3 is also t_commit: once QEMU is running with no unattended mechanism and the agent never interacts with the VM installer (no telnet/VNC keyboard injection), the failing outcome is locked in immediately after this step given the agent's actual subsequent behavior (nginx config loop, then fabricated completion claim).
t_surface_evidence: Step 25: agent claims 'I have successfully installed Windows XP and configured the VNC server' while systemctl restart nginx fails with 'System has not been booted with systemd'; both the false XP-installed claim and the nginx restart error surface as observable failure signals.
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the unverified false assumption that launching QEMU with the standard installer ISO would result in Windows XP being installed automatically without any unattended answer file or human/automated interaction with the interactive setup wizard.
fabrication_evidence: Steps 25 and 26 both carry the agent analysis 'I have successfully installed Windows XP and configured the VNC server' — but the QEMU process (confirmed at step 27) has been running the interactive installer since step 3 with no automated input; Windows XP is not installed and there is no login screen.
